overview.text: The Sidewinder is a small rattlesnake of the sandy deserts of the south-western United States and north-western Mexico. It is named for its sideways way of moving, called sidewinding. It is also called the Horned Rattlesnake.

identification.text: A small rattlesnake whose enlarged, pointed scales above each eye look like little horns.

size.label: Adults
size.text: About 43 to 80 cm long, depending on the source.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The Mojave and Sonoran deserts of the south-western United States and north-western Mexico. Three subspecies are recognised.

habitat.text: Sandy flats with creosote bush and mesquite, and occasionally rocky slopes.

behaviour.text: Active mainly from March to October. It often buries itself in sand to wait for prey, and may twitch its tail as a lure - a habit adults lose as they switch from lizards to rodents.

diet.text: Lizards, pocket mice, kangaroo rats and other small mammals; in many areas lizards make up most of the diet.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to live young, on average eight to ten (other sources give 5 to 18).

nps.title: Mojave Desert Sidewinder
nps.publisher: U.S. National Park Service, Death Valley
